title: Quilted prefetch savings notes
summary: Quick internal bench: compare a ‘quilted’ predictive-prefetch strategy vs baseline tiling and opportunistic prefetch. Goal = p90 latency under 220ms for small-chat workload while minimizing $/kq. Early numbers look promising but fragility around slot churn and cold starts remains.
body:
Context and goal:
- Team: product/optimize, probing a mid-complexity chat workload (short prompts, avg 70 tokens generated) typical of in-app assistants.
- Hypothesis: a quilted prefetch (light-weight intent classifier + staggered prefetched KV slices) can reduce p90 tail without large throughput losses compared to naive prefetch or pure tiling.

Test setup (short):
- HW: A100-like 80GB equiv nodes (prod-like), 8 nodes in cluster, single-tenant run.
- Model: open-llm-70b-quantized-mix (kv-friendly) pinned v3.
- Workload: synthetic mix derived from recent customer traces: 65% short queries (<=128 tokens), 25% mid (129-512), 10% long (>512). Session stickiness ~0.32.
- Concurrency: 1200 concurrent sessions, ramp 5m steady-state 20m.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latencies (ms), throughput QPS, $/1k queries (token-inferred cost model), slot-churn (new sessions causing cache misses), fragmentation-index (custom metric: fraction of almost-empty slots).

Configs compared:
1) baseline-tiling: fixed tiling window (4 session slots per shard), no predictive prefetch.
2) opportunistic-prefetch: prefetch on any session touch, full KV prefetch, no quilt logic.
3) quilted-prefetch-v1: intent classifier (micro model) predicts next-turn prefix with 60% precision/70% recall; prefetches partial KV slices staggered across 3ms offsets; partial fallbacks allowed.

Raw results (steady-state snapshot):
- Baseline-tiling:
  p50: 52ms, p90: 285ms, p99: 820ms, QPS: 5200, $/1kq: $1.12, slot-churn: 0.18, fragmentation-index: 0.41
- Opportunistic-prefetch:
  p50: 58ms, p90: 240ms, p99: 790ms, QPS: 5150, $/1kq: $1.35, slot-churn: 0.26, fragmentation-index: 0.58
- Quilted-prefetch-v1:
  p50: 50ms, p90: 198ms, p99: 640ms, QPS: 5250, $/1kq: $1.23, slot-churn: 0.14, fragmentation-index: 0.28

ASCII mini-chart (p90 vs $/1kq):
  (lower-left is better: low latency, low cost)

  $/1kq  |-------------------------------------------
  1.40   |   O (opportunistic)
  1.30   |  
  1.23   |        Q (quilted)
  1.12   |B (baseline)
  1.00   |
         +-----------------------------------------
            180   200   220   240   260   280   300
                         p90 latency (ms)

Interpretation / prose notes:
- Quilted prefetch delivers the best p90 (~198ms) while keeping cost closer to baseline than opportunistic. That suggests partial, staggered prefetch reduces tail without full KV churn.
- Opportunistic prefetch reduces tail relative to baseline but increases $/1kq significantly due to unnecessary full-KV prefetch churn (frag-index up).
- Baseline-tiling shows high p90/p99 under bursty tails despite decent $/1kq; tiling seems brittle to microbursts.
- Fragmentation-index correlates with cost increase; higher fragmentation => wasted slot capacity => higher per-query amortized cost.

Quick sensitivity checks (notes):
- When intent classifier precision drops to 42% (simulated drift), quilted p90 rises to ~235ms and $/1kq to $1.28; still better than opportunistic in latency but cost advantage narrows.
- Increasing session stickiness to 0.6 improves quilted p90 to 175ms and reduces $/1kq to $1.10 due to higher prefetch hit-rate.
- Cold-start heavy workload (90% new sessions) breaks opportunistic hard: $/1kq ~1.9, p90 ~360ms; quilted handles cold starts better because of staggered partial prefetching.

Operational caveats / fragility:
- The micro classifier adds a small operator dependency (model management, reprofiling cadence). Drift detection and periodic retraining needed.
- Stagger window timing is delicate; too aggressive causes contention on GPU kernel scheduling, too conservative misses windows. We need a smoothing layer in runtime to avoid oscillation.
- Edge cases: multimodal requests (embeds+chat) where intent classifier confidence is invalid; fall back to opportunistic may spike cost.

Next actions (short list):
- (1) Run longer 6h soak with production-weighted customer traces (including multimodal) and measure cost drift. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2029-05-20.
- (2) Add a cheap on-device fallback: when classifier confidence below 0.25, do a mini-prefix prefetch (50% slice) to reduce catastrophic misses. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2029-05-24.
- (3) Prototype runtime smoothing (exponential backoff of stagger rhythm) to reduce scheduling contention. Owner: Riley. ETA: 2029-05-17.

Open questions / discussion points for the sync:
- Is ~10–12% cost premium acceptable if p90 improves by ~25–30% for customer SLAs? Product needs to weigh uplift vs price sensitivity.
- How to instrument fragmentation-index in Console (low-effort metric)? Suggested panel: slot-fill histogram + fragmentation-index timeseries.
- Can Dedicated customers opt into quilted mode as a toggle (helps signal and mitigate cost shock)?

Notes-to-self: include a small artifact with code snippets for classifier eval and a notebook to reproduce the ascii scatter. Also link to the jitter/slot-scheduler PR once ready.

- initial experiment PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prefetch-experiments/pull/92
